newsitem.title: USA: White House plans no further capital gains tax cut.
newsitem.headline: White House plans no further capital gains tax cut.

text.p: The Clinton administration has no intention of proposing any additional capital gains tax cuts beyond their proposal to extend the exemption for gains on home sales of up to $500,000 per couple, White House economic adviser Gene Sperling told reporters on Friday.
He also made clear that while the White House is studying proposals on improving the CPI as a cost of living measure, it had no timetable on what the next step would be.

"The president believes very strongly in having a cost of living adjustment and he believes it should be based on the best broad-based technical agreement possible and it shouldn't be done for political or budgetary reasons," he said.
"We are studying different suggestions, we are studing different reports and we do not have any exact timetable," he added.
Sperling was upbeat about the reception on Capitol Hill to the Clinton Budget, saying it was being viewed in a largely constructive way compared to experiences of prior years.

"I think having Chairmen Kasich and Domenici, whatever their criticism, acknowledging that the president's budget is a serious one, that it's alive on arrival, is a sea-change over the last couple of years," he said.
